CHIEF COMPLAINT
Referral from emergency room for evaluation of esophagitis; history of chest pain three months ago.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Betty Hill is a new patient presenting with a referral from the ER for evaluation of esophagitis. She reports that approximately three months ago in early October 2020, she experienced sharp chest pain located in the center of her chest behind her breastbone. The pain occurred randomly and lasted for four days. Nothing she did relieved the symptoms, so she went to the emergency room. The pain was worse with eating. She also experienced difficulty swallowing during this time. She was unable to tolerate the pain after four days and sought emergency care. At the ER, she underwent an EKG and blood tests, which were all normal. She was referred to gastroenterology based on suspicion of a GI etiology. The chest pain and swallowing difficulty both resolved approximately three days after the ER visit. She has been asymptomatic for the past three months but reports feeling like something is wrong. She denies abdominal pain and reports normal bowel movements. She notes that she was undergoing a stressful job transition at the time of her symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies heartburn or indigestion. Denies abdominal pain. Reports normal bowel movements. Denies any current symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Uterine fibroids
Anemia
Cholecystectomy (several years ago)

MEDICATIONS
Not documented.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
No known family history of GI problems.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Currently attempting weight loss. Recent job transition three months ago associated with significant stress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Abdomen: Soft, non-distended. Mild tenderness to light palpation in bilateral upper abdominal quadrants. No tenderness in lower abdomen. No rebound or guarding. Otherwise normal examination.

RESULTS
ER cardiac workup: Normal (EKG and blood tests).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Patient presents with history of acute chest pain three months ago with associated dysphagia. Differential diagnosis includes GERD, dyspepsia, esophagitis, musculoskeletal etiologies, and anxiety. Given that symptoms occurred during stressful job transition and have completely resolved, suspect anxiety-related etiology with possible musculoskeletal contribution. Cardiac etiology has been ruled out with normal ER workup. EGD versus conservative monitoring was discussed. Patient elected to defer endoscopy and self-monitor for symptom recurrence. Will call office if any additional episodes of pain or other concerning symptoms develop. Follow-up as needed for GI complaints.
